definitions.explanation: A soft pink color reminiscent of peach blossoms. One of the traditional Japanese color names.
Used figuratively to describe matters related to love, romance, or sexual affairs. Similar to English 'rosy' in the romantic sense.

examples.japanese: {桃色|ももいろ}のリボンをつけた。
examples.english: I put on a pink ribbon.

examples.japanese: {空|そら}が{桃色|ももいろ}に{染|そ}まった。
{春|はる}の{庭|にわ}には{桃色|ももいろ}の{花|はな}がたくさん{咲|さ}いている。
examples.english: Many pink flowers bloom in the spring garden.

examples.japanese: {桃色|ももいろ}の{噂|うわさ}が{広|ひろ}まった。
あの{二人|ふたり}は{桃色|ももいろ}の{関係|かんけい}らしい。
examples.english: Those two apparently have a romantic relationship.

examples.japanese: {芸能|げいのう}{人|じん}の{桃色|ももいろ}スキャンダルがニュースになった。
examples.english: The celebrity's love scandal made the news.

notes:
USAGE:
As a color term, {桃色|ももいろ} is a traditional Japanese color name referring to a soft pink. In modern usage, ピンク is more commonly used for the color pink in everyday conversation, while {桃色|ももいろ} retains a more traditional or literary feel.

The figurative sense — romantic or amorous — appears in set phrases like {桃色|ももいろ}の{噂|うわさ} (romantic rumor) and {桃色|ももいろ}スキャンダル (love scandal). This usage is somewhat old-fashioned but still understood.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {桃色|ももいろ}の{噂|うわさ}: romantic rumor
- {桃色|ももいろ}スキャンダル: love scandal
- {桃色|ももいろ}に{染|そ}まる: to turn pink
